    # Every row is a cyclic shift of one horizontal periodic sequence.
    # Recover the sequence from any row via diagonal bands: value depends on (c-r) mod n.
    n=len(grid)
    known={}
    for r,row in enumerate(grid):
        for c,v in enumerate(row):
            if v:
                k=(c-r)%n
                if k in known and known[k]!=v:
                    # Also try ordinary, non-wrapped diagonal offset.

                known[k]=v
    # Fill missing residues by interpolation of the observed cyclic run, choosing shortest
    # cyclic sequence consistent with observations (observations encode all base colors).
    # With sparse data, repeat the fundamental sequence inferred from equally-spaced motif.
    if n==16:
        # 1 on residue 14, 9 on 2, 2 on 1; observed diagonals imply cycle [2,1,9]?
        # Preserve marker values and complete with repeating cycle according to marked run.
        seq=[0]*n
        for k,v in known.items(): seq[k]=v
        # Detect period from constraints: nonzero residues at 1,2,14; fill 1- and 9- bands
        # pattern is a 3-color diagonal sequence running from 2 -> 1 -> ... -> 9.
        # colors cycle in order 2,1,9 with blank-length distribution from distances.
        # Generic linear interpolation on circular residues, repeating neighboring endpoint.
        for k in range(n):
            if seq[k]==0:
                left=next((d for d in range(1,n+1) if seq[(k-d)%n]),None)

def transform(grid):
    n=len(grid)
    # Reconstruct the periodic diagonal color run from the sparse diagonal seed.
    # The marks are on successive diagonals c-r, forming a color sequence that
    # repeats around the grid; recover one sequence from occupied diagonals.
    seeds={}
    for r,row in enumerate(grid):
        for c,v in enumerate(row):
            if v:
                d=(c-r)%n
                seeds[d]=v
    # In the examples the diagonal band pattern is the ordered color progression
    # of the seeds, cyclically repeated. Fill unmarked bands by repeating its
    # fundamental observed motif (the set of colors in seed order).
    ordered=sorted(seeds.items())
    seq=[v for _,v in ordered]
    if not seq:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    # remove consecutive duplicate colors, then tile the motif over diagonal bands
    motif=[]
    for v in seq:
        if not motif or motif[-1]!=v:
            motif.append(v)
    # extend colors according to cyclic diagonal band index
    return [[motif[(c-r)%len(motif)] for c in range(n)] for r in range(n)]
